Let \(a=2015x,\ b=2015y\), with \(\gcd(x,y)=1\). Then \(a+b=2015(x+y)\), and the divisibility condition becomes
\[
x+y \mid 2015^{2015}\bigl((x-y)^{2016}+y^{2016}\bigr).
\]
Let \(s=x+y\). Modulo \(s\), \(x\equiv -y\), so
\[
(x-y)^{2016}+y^{2016}\equiv (2^{2016}+1)y^{2016}\pmod s.
\]
Since \(\gcd(s,y)=1\), this implies
\[
s\mid 2015^{2015}(2^{2016}+1).
\]
Thus the smallest possible \(s>1\) is the smallest prime divisor of \(2015^{2015}(2^{2016}+1)\). This number is odd, not divisible by \(3\), but divisible by \(5\). Hence the minimum is \(s=5\).

Therefore
\[
\min(a+b)=2015\cdot 5=10075.
\]

\[
\boxed{10075}
\]
